name: Mahimabhatta
dates_notes: Mahimabhaṭṭa is commonly placed around the turn of the eleventh century, principally by his engagement with earlier dhvani theory and by later reception. Precise dates are not secure.
sub_school: Semantic and inferential criticism of dhvani

lineage_polemical.note: The Vyaktiviveka challenges the need for an independent semantic power of suggestion in the account of poetic meaning.

core_thesis: Mahimabhaṭṭa is the most important sustained critic of the claim that poetic suggestion requires an independent semantic power called *vyañjanā*. In the *Vyaktiviveka*, he argues that effects assigned to suggestion should instead be explained through established linguistic operations and inferential understanding. His account of rasa is therefore pivotal: aesthetic appreciation is not denied, but its intelligibility is analyzed without granting dhvani the foundational status given it by Ānandavardhana and Abhinavagupta. The work preserves a serious internal alternative within Sanskrit poetics, not merely a rejected prelude to the later dhvani consensus.

engaged_works.title: Vyakti-Viveka
engaged_works.composition_dates_notes: Conventionally dated around the turn of the eleventh century.
engaged_works.ascription_notes: Securely transmitted as Mahimabhaṭṭa's treatise on poetic meaning.

ascription_evidence.description: The work is standardly recognized as Mahimabhaṭṭa's major intervention in the dhvani debate.

engaged_works.summary: A sustained critique of dhvani theory. The work examines the linguistic mechanisms invoked to explain suggested meaning and argues against treating vyañjanā as an additional word-power. Its analysis of rasa and interpretation makes it a major source for the inferential alternative to the dhvani account of poetic experience.
